sections.h2: Anne Arundel County at a glance
sections.html: Just south of Baltimore, Anne Arundel County fronts the Chesapeake Bay, and its seat Annapolis doubles as Maryland's capital. About 588,261 people lived here in 2020. Water covers 173 of the county's 588 square miles (29 percent), which is why creeks, rivers and shoreline lots define so much of the housing. Fort Meade, BWI airport and state government keep buyers coming, and commuters reach Baltimore and Washington by road, light rail or MARC.

The state assessments office, SDAT, revalued the county as of January 1, 2026. Here is how much value moved over the three years.

Measure (Jan. 1, 2023 to Jan. 1, 2026)Anne Arundel County
Combined full cash value$46.52 billion to $53.53 billion (up 15.1%)
Residential value$31.23 billion to $36.24 billion (up 16.0%)
Commercial value$15.28 billion to $17.29 billion (up 13.1%)
Residential properties that rose in value98.98%

Higher values are spread in equal steps over three years, while a drop applies in full for the 2026 tax year. To contest a value, you have 45 days from the date on the Notice of Assessment. Start with SDAT, then go to the county's Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board, and last to the Maryland Tax Court. On a principal residence, the homestead credit holds down how fast taxable assessment can grow: 10 percent is the state ceiling, and some local governments set it lower.

The annual bill goes out in July to the mailing address SDAT has on file. It is payable without interest starting July 1 and must be settled by September 30. If you live in the house as your principal residence, you may pay in two halves, the first by September 30 and the second by December 31.

The fiscal year 2027 bill, covering July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027, carries a 0.87 percent service charge on whatever is left for the second installment. Maryland lets local governments charge up to 1.65 percent, so this county stays under the limit. A single payment by September 30 avoids the charge altogether.

  • The state portion is $0.112 per $100 of taxable assessment.
  • Addresses inside the City of Annapolis add $0.738 per $100.
  • If a lender escrows your taxes and you prefer a single annual payment, notify the lender by May 1.
  • A homestead credit application filed by December 31 starts working July 1 of the next year.

Before you estimate what you owe, ask the Real Property Tax Division which county rate applies to your address.

The Real Property Tax Division, 44 Calvert Street, Room 110, Annapolis, answers billing questions. Reach it Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., at (410) 222-1736 or realproperty@aacounty.org. Values and ownership records sit with SDAT.

  • Finance Department customer service: (410) 222-1144.
  • Land Records, for deeds and liens: (410) 222-1425.
  • SDAT, to change ownership or a mailing address: (410) 974-5709.
  • Cashier's offices, including the one in Glen Burnie, are open Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Outside those hours, drop a sealed check in the yellow box and it is handled the next business day.

Did you pay a bill on a house you have already sold? Ask the office about a refund. Credits left after a bill is adjusted are returned as quickly as possible.

Recording a deed here costs a county recordation tax of $7.00 per thousand of value, with the base rounded up to the next $500. The county transfer tax is 1.0 percent for prices through $999,999.99 and 1.5 percent from $1 million up. The Recordation and Transfer Tax Division collects both and must endorse any instrument that could be taxed before it goes on record.

Make checks payable to Anne Arundel County. The state's transfer tax and recording fees run through the Land Records Office at (410) 222-1425, which also accepts e-recording. Refund claim forms for both taxes and an affidavit for certain transactions are posted by the county. The sales contract decides who pays which tax, so have your title company list each charge before you accept an offer.

sections.h2: Waterfront sellers and the Critical Area
sections.html:
Land and water within 1,000 feet of tidal waters make up the Critical Area, and the rules can limit what a buyer is allowed to do with a lot.

  • The Buffer extends 100 feet landward from tidal waters, tributary stream banks and tidal wetland boundaries. Disturbing it generally takes an approved variance.
  • Removing any tree or vegetation, even a dead tree, requires an approved Vegetation Management Plan.
  • Grading disturbances over 5,000 square feet need a grading permit.
  • In limited development and resource conservation areas, impervious surface is capped at 15 to 31 percent of the site.

The county's Critical Area Planner of the Day is at the Heritage Complex, 2664 Riva Road, Annapolis, (410) 222-7960. Own a pier, deck or bulkhead near the water? Gather its permits before you list, and ask the title company whether any disclosure applies.

Tax left unpaid turns into a lien, and the county can auction that lien at its June tax sale on a date the Controller picks. You still own the house afterward. The winning bidder gets a tax lien certificate and may foreclose if the debt is never cleared.

Ahead of the sale the collector has to mail you a notice at least 30 days before the first advertisement, which then runs weekly for four weeks. The buyer can start foreclosure six months after the sale, or nine for an owner-occupied home, and the certificate dies if nothing is filed within two years. To redeem, you pay interest of 1.5 percent per month, so every month of delay adds to the payoff.

Homeowners with limited income, or who are elderly or disabled, may be eligible for the state's Homeowner Protection Program. The State Tax Sale Ombudsman sees people by appointment at 123 Market Place, Baltimore.

Owing money to the county does not block a sale, as long as the balance is cleared by closing. Get the amount from the Real Property Tax Division, and move before the June tax sale if you are behind. The title company can wire the county out of your proceeds.

  1. Request a payoff figure for each open bill.
  2. Collect permits for any waterfront structures and any Critical Area approvals.
  3. Have the title company spell out the recordation and transfer taxes.
  4. Close, and the title company pays the county from the proceeds.

Our offers are for the house as it stands, so a worn bulkhead or an old deck is not something you have to fix first. Send the address by call or text and we will say what we can pay.

faqs.q: When are Anne Arundel County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Payment without interest opens July 1 and closes September 30. A principal residence may be paid half by September 30 and half by December 31.

faqs.q: What is the semiannual service charge in Anne Arundel County?
faqs.a: It is 0.87 percent of the second installment balance for fiscal year 2027. One full payment by September 30 avoids it.

faqs.q: How do I appeal an Anne Arundel County assessment?
faqs.a: Send it to SDAT within 45 days of the Notice of Assessment. Still unhappy? Take it to the county appeals board, then the Maryland Tax Court.

faqs.q: What are the transfer tax rates in Anne Arundel County?
faqs.a: Transfer tax is 1.0 percent through $999,999.99 and 1.5 percent at $1 million or more. Recordation tax is $7.00 per thousand, rounded up to the next $500.

faqs.q: Does the Critical Area affect selling a house near the water?
faqs.a: It can. A lot within 1,000 feet of tidal water is in the Critical Area, with a 100 foot buffer plus vegetation and grading rules that a buyer needs to know about.
